CAREER_ADVICE.TITLE: Career Advice
CAREER_ADVICE.SUB-TITLE: Tips to grow your developer career

GIT_DEBUGGING.TITLE: Master Git and debugging tools
GIT_DEBUGGING.DESC: Knowing how to bisect bugs, write clear commit messages, and use your browser’s debugger efficiently saves more time than typing fast ever will.

BUSINESS_IMPACT.TITLE: Understand the business impact
BUSINESS_IMPACT.DESC: Great developers don't just write code; they solve user and business problems. Always ask why a feature is being built before deciding how to build it.

TESTS.TITLE: Write tests for your future self
TESTS.DESC: Automated tests aren't a chore—they are safety nets. They give you the confidence to refactor and push changes without breaking existing functionality.

CODE_REVIEWS.TITLE: Embrace constructive code reviews
CODE_REVIEWS.DESC: Feedback on your pull requests isn't a critique of your intelligence. Treat code reviews as a free learning opportunity and a way to elevate team standards.

SOFT_SKILLS.TITLE: Improve your soft skills
SOFT_SKILLS.DESC: Technical chops get you hired, but empathy, active listening, and clear written communication are what make you a senior engineer people want to work with.

STEP_AWAY.TITLE: Learn to step away when stuck
STEP_AWAY.DESC: Staring at a bug for hours often yields diminishing returns. A short walk or a good night's sleep allows your brain to find solutions passively.

DOCUMENTATION.TITLE: Document as you go
DOCUMENTATION.DESC: Good documentation saves hours of onboarding and troubleshooting for your team. If you struggled to figure something out, write down the fix for others.

WORK_LIFE_BALANCE.TITLE: Prioritize work-life balance
WORK_LIFE_BALANCE.DESC: Burnout is the biggest threat to a long software engineering career. Pace yourself, set clear boundaries, and maintain hobbies outside of technology.
